newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition forms new government.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition forms new government.

text.p: Opponents of Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia have formed a new government under ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani, opposition sources in Islamabad said on Tuesday.

They said Rabbani had named a new government after meeting Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, a representative of the Hazara militia chief Karim Khalili, and other opposition figures in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif on Thursday.
Rabbani's former military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, an old rival of Dostum, did not attend the meeting.
The defence ministry was allocated to Dostum and the finance ministry to Khalili, though it was not immediately clear if they would serve personally in those posts.
The sources did not have a full list of posts in the new government, but said the three ethnic groups opposed to the Taleban -- Uzbeks, Tajiks and Hazaras -- were all represented.
The Taleban, who draw their strength mainly from the ethnic Pashtun community, captured Kabul from Masood's forces in September and have vowed to overrun the opposition-held north.
The Taleban administration in Kabul, which has so far failed to win international recognition, has repeatedly demanded that it be recognised as the legitimate government of Afghanistan.
Taleban forces are locked in combat with opposition forces led by Masood, Dostum and Khalili on frontlines north of Kabul and in the northwestern province of Badghis.
The three opposition leaders formed a loose military pact after the fall of Kabul, but diplomats say tensions between them continue to hamper their battle against the Taleban.
